title.rendered: Resting in His Love: He Rejoices Over You with Singing | Living from Rest, Day 14

excerpt.rendered: Zephaniah 3:17 says God Himself quiets us with His love and rejoices over us with singing. Day 14 closes the series with the deepest rest of all.

content.rendered:
You are not just loved by a God who tolerates you. You are loved by a God who sings over you. This is where the series lands: the Father who rests in His love over His children.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, November 14, 2026 | Living from Rest, Day 14

Today’s Scripture

“The Lord your God in your midst, the Mighty One, will save; He will rejoice over you with gladness, He will quiet you with His love, He will rejoice over you with singing.”
Zephaniah 3:17 (NKJV)

“It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows; for so He gives His beloved sleep.”
Psalm 127:2 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Fourteen mornings ago we began with an invitation. Come to Me, all you who labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Over this fortnight we have walked from Matthew to Hebrews, from Psalm 23 to Mark 4, from Exodus 33 to Isaiah 30 to Psalm 46 to John 15 to Philippians 4 to 2 Chronicles 20 to Exodus 14. The same note has sounded through every passage. Rest is not an achievement; it is a posture. It is a Person. It is a settled union with the God who loves us.

Today, the series lands where it was always going to land. Zephaniah 3:17, in the NKJV, says, “The Lord your God in your midst, the Mighty One, will save; He will rejoice over you with gladness, He will quiet you with His love, He will rejoice over you with singing.” The AMPC says, “The Lord your God is in the midst of you, a Mighty One, a Savior [Who saves]! He will rest [in silent satisfaction] and in His love He will be silent and make no mention [of past sins, or even recall them].” The TPT says, “He will rejoice over you with gladness, in his love he will renew you with his love and dance over you with shouts of joy!”

Linger on each phrase. The Lord your God is in your midst. He is not watching from a distance. He is near. The Mighty One, will save. This is not a sentimental God; this is the Rescuer with the arm of a Saviour. He will rejoice over you with gladness. He is not merely patient with you. He is glad about you. He will quiet you with His love. Not with explanations. Not with achievement. With love. He will rejoice over you with singing. The God of the universe sings over His children. Let that settle.

And Psalm 127:2 adds the final line. The worker who tries to earn rest by rising early, staying late, and eating the bread of sorrows is working against the grain of the gospel. “For so He gives His beloved sleep.” Beloved. That is the operative word. You are not a hired hand negotiating overtime. You are a beloved child whose Father has already written the paycheck in blood.

Save this page. Print it. Pin it. Pray it over your children before school. Pray it over your spouse at night. Pray it over your own heart in the mirror. Living from rest means living from being loved. He is in your midst. He is Mighty. He saves. He is glad. He quiets you with His love. And He is singing over you right now.

What the Series Was Really About

Rest is a Person before it is a practice. You rest because of who He is.

Rest is received before it is lived. You cannot live from what you have not received.

Rest is a Father’s delight over His child. You are not tolerated; you are sung over.

Declaration

Lord, I thank You that You are in my midst, the Mighty One who has saved me (Zephaniah 3:17). Thank You that You rejoice over me with gladness, quiet me with Your love, and rejoice over me with singing. I am Your beloved, and You give Your beloved sleep (Psalm 127:2). I will not rise early, sit up late, and eat the bread of sorrows to earn what You have already given me. I live, work, and love from Your rest, under Your song, inside Your love. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
